questions.solution:
Synthetic drugs, brompheniramine (Dimetapp) act as antihistamines.

Antihistamines are drugs which treat hay fever and other allergies. Typically, people take antihistamines as an inexpensive, not patented, drug that can be bought without a prescription and relieves from nasal congestion, sneezing, or hives caused by pollen, dust mites, or animal allergy with few side effects.

We know that drugs help us diagnose and cure numerous illnesses. But any drug consumed by humans can actually have two kinds of effects - therapeutic effects and side effects. The goal is to prescribe the ideal drug, the one that only has a therapeutic effect.

questions.q: In an experiment to verify Stokes law, a small spherical ball of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>r</mi></math> and density <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>ρ</mi></math> falls under gravity through a distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>h</mi></math> in air before entering a tank of water. If the terminal velocity of the ball inside water is same as its velocity just before entering the water surface, then the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>h</mi></math> is proportional to: (ignore viscosity of air)
questions.solution:
The velocity of ball just before striking the surface of water is given by using kinematical equation of motion under the gravity

v2=u2-2gy

⇒v2=-2g(-h)

⇒v=2gh  ...(1) 

Now, the terminal velocity of spherical ball inside the water tank is given by,

vT=29r2(ρ-σ)gη  ...(2)

After falling through h the velocity of ball should be equal to its terminal velocity.

From equation (1) and (2) we get,

⇒2gh=29r2(ρ-σ)gη

Squaring the above equation, we get

⇒h=281r4g(ρ-σ)2η2

⇒h∝r4

questions.q: A radioactive nucleus decays by two different processes. The half-life for the first process is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> and that for the second is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>. The effective half-life of the nucleus is close to:
questions.solution:
Using the equation of radioactive decay law,

-dNdt=λ1N+λ2N  ...(1)

-dNdt=λ1+λ2N  ...(2)

Where,

-dNdt is the rate of decay

λ1, λ2 are decay constant for two different processes

N is the number of atoms.

Now applying the decay law for the combine process, we get

-dNdt=λeffN  ...(3)

Equating equation (1) and (2) we get

λeff=λ1+λ2  ...(4)

Now the half life of the radioactive nucleus is given by,

λ=ln2T  ...(5)

Where, T is the half life of the radioactive nucleus

Using equation (5) equation (4) becomes,

ln2T=ln2T1+ln2T2

1T=1T1+1T2

1T=110+1100=11100

⇒T=10011≈9 s

questions.q: A ring is hung on a nail. It can oscillate, without slipping or sliding (i) in its plane with a time period <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>T</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and (ii) back and forth in a direction perpendicular to its plane, with a period <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>T</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math>. The ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><msub><mi>T</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><msub><mi>T</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mfrac></math> will be :
questions.solution:
The time period of oscillation of physical pendulum is given by

T=2πIMgl  ...(1)

Where, I is the moment of inertia of ring about given axis and l is the distance of centre of mass of ring from the axis of rotation.

Moment of inertia of ring in its plane is given by

I1=Ic+ Md2=MR2+MR2=2MR2

Moment of inertia of ring perpendicular to its plane is given by

I2=Ic+ Md2=MR22+MR2=32MR2

Now the ratio of time period is given by 

T1T2=I1I2

⇒T1T2=2MR232MR2

⇒T1T2=43=23
